prior_attempt.rejection: The first correction separated state borders from arrows, but treated stateArrowColor as unconditionally more specific than ArrowColor. Java normalizes both spellings to the same arrowColor style property, so their declarations override in source order.

second_rejection.rejection: The renderer's unified reverse alias lookup was correct for distinct parsed keys, but parse::collapse_reassigned_skinparams had already collapsed repeated raw spellings independently. It retained each raw key's first position, so a later repeated stateArrowColor could still sort before an intervening ArrowColor even though Java canonicalizes all family-arrow aliases before updating one map entry.

invariant: Java resolves state-image borders and state-diagram arrows from sibling style signatures. FromSkinparamToStyle maps stateBorderColor to root.element.stateDiagram.state LineColor. Before either its parameter map or style conversion sees a declaration, SkinParam.cleanForKeySlow lowercases and trims the key, removes underscores and dots, rewrites sequenceParticipant/sequenceActor aliases, rewrites every activity/class/component/object/sequence/state/usecase Arrow prefix to the shared arrow prefix, and rewrites a terminal align to alignment. SkinParam.setParam then processes these canonical keys in source order through a LinkedHashMap: an alias-equivalent reassignment changes the existing entry's value without moving its first insertion position, while style conversion observes the new value immediately. Thus stateArrowColor and ArrowColor are one arrowColor identity, no matter how often or with what case they alternate, and the last declaration sets root.element.stateDiagram.arrow LineColor. GraphvizImageBuilder and SvekEdge independently merge that arrow signature and derive the shaft and arrowhead Rainbow from it. The arrow signature may inherit the root or theme line color, but never the state sibling's explicit LineColor. A per-link color remains the final arrow-only override.
causal_divergence: Commit 8289f2e0 correctly performs one renderer lookup across the two arrow aliases, but parse::collapse_reassigned_skinparams compares raw keys case-insensitively rather than comparing Java's cleanForKey identities. In an alternating sequence stateArrowColor, ArrowColor, stateArrowColor, ArrowColor, stateArrowColor, Rust collapses each raw spelling into a separate first-position slot and updates only its value. The final state-prefixed value remains in the earlier slot, so the renderer's reverse scan incorrectly selects the later-position global slot. Java canonicalizes all five declarations to arrowColor before replacement, leaving one entry with the final value. The rejected alternating-alias heldout isolates this as eight color-only shaft and arrowhead differences.
planned_change: Model SkinParam.cleanForKeySlow's ordinary-key identity in the parser's reassignment collapse: trim and lowercase, remove underscore and dot separators, normalize sequence aliases, normalize every family-arrow prefix to arrow, and normalize a terminal align to alignment. Compare declarations by that canonical identity before applying LinkedHashMap-style first-position/last-value replacement, while retaining the first stored spelling for compatibility with existing renderer lookups and leaving RustUML's double-underscore internal metadata ordered and uncanonicalized. Keep the renderer's one reverse source-order lookup, stateBorderColor isolation, root/theme fallback, and per-transition final override. Add parser tests for alternating mixed-case aliases and canonical separator/alignment identities, and preserve every opposite-order, border-only, changed-count, and local-link heldout. Do not special-case state fixtures, colors, counts, or geometry.
